QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r1.claim: Al-Tha'labi cites the water, fire, and salt report, which Ibn Majah records; Qurtubi says its chain is weak, and it is the twelfth interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r1.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي في تفسيره، وخرجه ابن ماجه في سننه. وفي إسناده لين وهو القول الثاني عشر.

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r2.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r2.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests ma'un means assistance through an act that is small but treated as burdensome.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r2.anchor: الماوردي: ويحتمل أنه المعونة بما خف فعله وقد ثقله الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة مولى ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r3.claim: Ikrima says that refusing one household object alone does not merit woe; the condemnation concerns combining neglected prayer, showiness, and stinginess with ma'un.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r3.anchor: وقيل لعكرمة مولى ابن عباس: من منع شيئا من المتاع كان له الويل؟ فقال: لا، ولكن من جمع ثلاثهن فله الويل يعني: ترك الصلاة، والرياء، والبخل بالماعون.

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r5.claim: A sincere Muslim is unlikely to combine all three traits, though withholding a necessary aid, like abandoning prayer, earns a share of the rebuke.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r5.anchor: ويبعد أن توجد من مسلم محقق، وإن وجد بعضها فيلحقه جزء من التوبيخ، وذلك في منع الماعون إذا تعين

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r6.claim: Withholding assistance is reprehensible as a matter of good character only outside necessity.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-7#2/r6.anchor: إنما يكون منعا قبيحا في المروءة في غير حال الضرورة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r1.claim: Al-ma'un means aid, kindness, and goodness for fellow human beings and God's servants; withholding it shows prayer's intended effects are absent.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r1.anchor: فهم يمنعون الماعون . يمنعون المعونة والبر والخير عن إخوانهم في البشرية

QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r2.claim: If people truly established prayer for God, they would not withhold help from His servants; their treatment of others tests whether worship is sincere and accepted.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r2.anchor: ولو كانوا يقيمون الصلاة حقا لله ما منعوا العون عن عباده ، فهذا هو محك العبادة الصادقة المقبولة عند الله

QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r3.claim: The warned worshippers perform empty motions for show without devotion or effect on their hearts and actions, so their prayer becomes a sin awaiting punishment.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r3.anchor: إنما أدوا حركات لا روح فيها . ولم يتجردوا لله فيها . إنما أدوها رياء

QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r4.claim: God's call to faith and worship serves human flourishing, not any need of God: it seeks pure hearts, happiness, mutual care, generosity, love, and brotherhood.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r4.anchor: إنه لا يريد منهم شيئا لذاته سبحانه - فهو الغني - إنما يريد صلاحهم هم أنفسهم

QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r5.claim: Qutb asks why humanity wanders into dark confusion when divine goodness and mercy offer a clear route to an elevated, generous life.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:7/r5.anchor: أين تذهب لتخبط في متاهات الجاهلية المظلمة النكدة وأمامها هذا النور في مفرق الطريق

ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r3.claim: Al-māʿūn means things that are useful.

ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r4.claim: In pre-Islamic usage, māʿūn included any useful item, even an axe, bucket, pot, or fire striker—anything useful, little or much; al-Aʿshā’s poem uses the word māʿūnihi.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r4.anchor: والماعون في الجاهلية ما فيه منفعة حتى الفأس والدلو والقدر والقداحة

ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r5.speaker: الأعشى
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r5.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line witnesses māʿūn as a useful possession or provision offered generously.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r5.anchor: قال الأعشى: بأجود منه بماعونه. . . إذا ما سماؤهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r6.claim: In Islam, māʿūn is said to mean zakat and obedience; al-Rāʿī’s verse mentions people withholding their māʿūn and neglecting the declaration of God’s oneness.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r6.anchor: والماعون في الإسلام قيل هو الزكاة والطاعة. قال الراعي.

ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r7.speaker: الراعي
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāʿī’s poem uses māʿūnahum while describing people who withhold it and neglect tahlīl, supporting the gloss of ritual obligation and obedience.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367#2/r7.anchor: قال الراعي. قومي على الإسلام لما يمنعوا. . . ماعونهم

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r1.claim: After discussing prayer, the passage follows by mentioning the withholding of aid.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r1.anchor: ثم لما شرح أمر الصلاة أعقبه بذكر الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r2.speaker: أبو بكر وعلي وابن عباس وابن الحنفية وابن عمر والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r2.anchor: وهو قول أبي بكر وعلي وابن عباس وابن الحنفية وابن عمر والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك : هو الزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r3.speaker: أبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r3.claim: A report from Ubay says reciting Surat al-Ma'un brings forgiveness for one who pays zakat, which suggests that “al-ma'un” means zakat.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r3.anchor: وفي حديث أبي : ( من قرأ سورة

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r4.claim: The placement after prayer supports the zakat interpretation, since zakat naturally follows prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r4.anchor: ولأن الله تعالى ذكره عقيب الصلاة ، فالظاهر أن يكون ذلك هو الزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r5.claim: Most commentators say “al-ma'un” names ordinary useful items that people customarily lend and whose refusal marks bad character, such as an axe, pot, bucket, fire striker, sieve, or adze; the list also includes salt, water, and fire.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول أكثر المفسرين ، أن { الماعون } اسم لما لا يمنع في العادة ويسأله الفقير والغني

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r6.claim: A report says three things may not be withheld: water, fire, and salt.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r6.anchor: فإنه روى : ( ثلاثة لا يحل منعها ، الماء والنار والملح )

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r7.claim: Ordinary examples include letting a neighbor bake in one's oven or store belongings at one's home briefly.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك أن يلتمس جارك أن يخبز في تنورك ، أو يضع متاعه عندك يوما أو نصف يوم

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r8.claim: “Ma'un” is a diminutive thing, from “ma'n”; zakat is called this because a small fraction is taken from a larger holding, and customary borrowed tools also bear the name.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r8.anchor: الماعون فاعول من المعن . وهو الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r9.claim: On the everyday-items reading, the verse rebukes stinginess over small things, a trait of hypocrites; the author connects it to warnings about misers and those who withhold good.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r9.anchor: وعلى هذا التقدير يكون معنى الآية الزجر عن البخل بهذه الأشياء القليلة ، فإن البخل بها يكون في نهاية الدناءة والركاكة ، والمنافقون كانوا كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r10.speaker: العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r10.claim: Scholars praise keeping extra household necessities to lend neighbors, rather than limiting oneself to the obligatory minimum.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r10.anchor: قال العلماء : ومن الفضائل أن يستكثر الرجل في منزله مما يحتاج إليه الجيران ، فيعيرهم ذلك ولا يقتصر على الواجب

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r11.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r11.claim: Al-Farra reports an Arab usage equating “al-ma'un” with water and cites the line “يمج بعيره الماعون مجا” as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r11.anchor: قال الفراء : سمعت بعض العرب يقول : الماعون هو الماء وأنشدني فيه : يمج بعيره الماعون مجا

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r12.claim: Water may be singled out because it is most precious when absent and commonplace when present; people in Hell first ask for it, and it is among the first pleasures of Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r12.anchor: ولعله خصه بذلك لأن أعز مفقود وأرخص موجود ، وأول شيء يسأله أهل النار الماء

RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p108/r13.claim: A fourth view defines “al-ma'un” as willing obedience, as in the saying “restrain your camel until it gives you obedience.”

RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r1.claim: Razi prefers the broadest meaning: every act of obedience that is easy to perform, since this interpretation is more beneficial.
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الأولى أن يحمل على كل طاعة يخف فعلها لأنه أكثر فائدة

RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r2.claim: The contrast is that prayer belongs to God and al-ma'un belongs to people: hypocrites display to people what is due to God and conceal from people what is due to them, reversing proper conduct toward both.
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r2.anchor: كأنه تعالى يقول الصلاة لي والماعون للخلق

RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r3.claim: The explanation that God concealed the hypocrite's name is answered by saying Adam's lapse was named only after his death and coupled with repentance, as a lesson to his descendants.
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r3.anchor: والجواب : أنه تعالى ذكر زلة آدم لكن بعد موته مقرونا بالتوبة

RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r4.claim: Adam's small sin led to his expulsion from Paradise, so people should not expect entry after committing a major sin.
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r4.anchor: أنه أخرج من الجنة بسبب الصغيرة فكيف يطمعون في الدخول مع الكبيرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r5.claim: Naming Adam's lapse also honors him, since it was his only lapse and he repented with such repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r5.anchor: فإن وصف تلك الزلة رفعة له فإنه رجل لم يصدر عنه إلا تلك الزلة الواحدة ثم تاب عنها مثل هذه التوبة

RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r6.claim: In the closing prayer, Razi contrasts the present sura's hypocrites with the next sura's description of Muhammad: though short of Muhammad and his Companions in obedience, he prays that they remain unlike the hypocrites in evil and asks God's pardon.
RAZI-FULL:v32p109/r6.anchor: هذه السورة في ذكر المنافقين والسورة التي بعدها في صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فنحن وإن لم نصل في الطاعة إلى محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام وإلى أصحابه

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Māʿūn an early Makkan sūrah after al-Takāthur, though some assign vv. 4–7 to Madinah; since the whole sūrah addresses religious hypocrisy, it may all be Madinan, when hypocrisy could gain political advantage.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.anchor: commentators maintain that al-Māʿūn is an early Makkan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.claim: Religious hypocrisy is not treated as limited to Muslims alone.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.anchor: Nonetheless, hypocrisy in religion was not seen as limited to Muslims alone.

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from māʿūn in its last verse, broadly meaning kindness, charity, or assistance.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.anchor: The sūrah takes its name from the word māʿūn in the last verse, which in its widest sense indicates any act of kindness, charity, or assistance.

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.claim: The verse describes people who perform devotions well but fail to act kindly toward others.
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.anchor: This verse is understood to indicate those who perform their devotions well but do not act kindly toward others (IK).

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.speaker: widespread interpretation
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.claim: Māʿūn commonly means utensils or tools that neighbors share or lend, such as a pickax, pot, or bucket.
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.anchor: a widespread interpretation that sees it as an allusion to utensils or tools that people would share and lend to one another

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.claim: Other interpretations take māʿūn as anything beneficial, obligatory zakāh, property generally in Qurayshi dialect, or refusing guests.
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.anchor: It can also be seen as an allusion to anything in which there is benefit (Q). Many take refuse small kindnesses to indicate refusal to pay the obligatory zakāh

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.claim: All readings point to hypocrites' stinginess: they attend prayer lazily and spend reluctantly.
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.anchor: According to all of these interpretations, the verse indicates the stinginess exhibited by hypocrites, who only come to the prayer lazily, and only spend reluctantly

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed in the mission's early years, probably after surah 102; its title comes from al-ma'un in the last verse.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.anchor: revealed in the early years of the Prophet's mission (probably after surah 102), is derived from the word al-ma'un occurring in the last verse

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.speaker: some commentators
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.claim: Some commentators date verses 4–7 to Medina, but Asad rejects this view for lack of historical or textual evidence.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.anchor: The view of some commentators that verses 4-7 were revealed at Medina lacks all historical or textual evidence and may, therefore, be disregarded.

ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r1.claim: Al-ma'un includes small daily-use items and occasional kindnesses that help others with such things.
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r1.anchor: comprises the many small items needed for one's daily use, as well as the occasional acts of kindness consisting in helping out one's fellow-men with such items

ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r2.claim: More broadly, al-ma'un means aid or assistance in any difficulty.
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n4/r2.anchor: In its wider sense, it denotes "aid" or "assistance" in any difficulty

TAB-FULL:v24p666/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r1.claim: Maʿun is the benefit of any thing people possess; rainwater is also called maʿun. The verse describes people withholding benefits from others.
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] يقول: ويمنعون الناس منافع ما عندهم، وأصل الماعون من كل شيء منفعته؛ يقال للماء الذي ينزل من السحاب: ماعون

TAB-FULL:v24p666/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r2.claim: Al-Aʿsha's verse uses maʿun for the benefit supplied when rain falls, and another poet uses it for rain pouring from a cloud.
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r2.anchor: ومنه قول أعشى بني ثعلبة: [البحر المتقارب] بأجود منه بماعونه … إذا ما سماؤهم لم تغم

TAB-FULL:v24p666/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r3.speaker: عبيد الراعي
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r3.claim: A verse by Ubayd al-Raʿi uses maʿun for obedience and zakat, linking withholding it with neglecting praise of God.
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r3.anchor: وقال عبيد الراعي: [البحر الكامل] قوم على الإسلام لما يمنعوا … ماعونهم ويضيعوا التهليلا يعني بالماعون: الطاعة والزكاة.

TAB-FULL:v24p666/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r4.claim: Ali, in reports transmitted by Mujahid, interprets maʿun as zakat.
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: قال علي رضى الله عنه في قوله: {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: «الزكاة»

TAB-FULL:v24p666/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r5.claim: Mujahid also glosses maʿun as zakat.
TAB-FULL:v24p666/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: «الزكاة»

TAB-FULL:v24p668/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p668/r1.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p668/r1.claim: Ali's interpretation, transmitted through Mujahid, is that maʿun is obligatory charity or zakat.
TAB-FULL:v24p668/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، أن عليا رضي الله عنه كان يقول: " {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] الصدقة المفروضة "

TAB-FULL:v24p668/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p668/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v24p668/r2.claim: Ibn Umar interprets maʿun as zakat, the right owed on wealth, and rejects Ibn Masud's interpretation as loaned household items.
TAB-FULL:v24p668/r2.anchor: عن سلمة بن كهيل، عن أبي المغيرة، قال: سأل رجل ابن عمر: عن {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] ، قال: «هو المال الذي لا يؤدى حقه»

TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r1.anchor: عن سلمة، عن الضحاك، قال: «هي الزكاة»

TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says maʿun includes household implements people lend one another, such as an axe, pot, or bucket.
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي العبيدين، أنه قال لعبد الله: أخبرني عن {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] ؟ قال: «هو ما يتعاوره الناس بينهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r3.speaker: أصحاب محمد
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet's Companions spoke of maʿun as the axe, pot, and bucket that people need and share.
TAB-FULL:v24p670#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن حارثة بن مضرب، عن أبي العبيدين، عن عبد الله، " كنا أصحاب محمد نحدث أن الماعون: القدر والفأس والدلو "

TAB-FULL:v24p673/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p673/r1.speaker: أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v24p673/r1.claim: The Prophet's Companions identify maʿun as commonly shared household items such as an axe, bucket, and pot.
TAB-FULL:v24p673/r1.anchor: عن أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قالوا: " إن من الماعون: الفأس والدلو والقدر "

TAB-FULL:v24p673/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p673/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p673/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says maʿun is a pot, axe, and bucket, or other similar household things people use among themselves.
TAB-FULL:v24p673/r2.anchor: عن أبي العبيدين، قال: قال عبد الله: " {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] : القدر والفأس والدلو "

TAB-FULL:v24p675/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r1.claim: Ibn Masud interprets maʿun as everyday items people lend among themselves, including an axe, pot, and bucket.
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r1.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن الحارث بن سويد، عن عبد الله، أنه سئل عن {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] ، قال: " ما يتعاوره الناس بينهم: الفأس والدلو وشبهه "

TAB-FULL:v24p675/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r2.claim: Ibrahim says maʿun is the loan of people's household implements, such as an axe, pot, and bucket.
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم، أنه قال " هو عارية الناس: الفأس والقدر والدلو ونحو ذلك، يعني الماعون "

TAB-FULL:v24p675/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets maʿun as borrowing, with one report specifying an axe and bucket.
TAB-FULL:v24p675/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، مثله، قال: الفأس والدلو

TAB-FULL:v24p677/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says maʿun means household goods, and another report says it is the loan people provide to one another.
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: «متاع البيت»

TAB-FULL:v24p677/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that people differed over whether maʿun means zakat, obedience, or items lent to others.
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: " اختلف الناس في ذلك، فمنهم من قال: يمنعون الزكاة، ومنهم من قال: يمنعون الطاعة، ومنهم من قال: يمنعون العارية "

TAB-FULL:v24p677/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r3.claim: Ali combines withholding zakat with withholding lendable implements as meanings of maʿun.
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r3.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن الحارث، قال: قال علي رضي الله عنه: " {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] : منع الزكاة والفأس والدلو والقدر "

TAB-FULL:v24p677/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says maʿun is a loan or borrowed item.
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r4.anchor: عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت، عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] : العارية "

TAB-FULL:v24p677/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r5.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r5.claim: Abu Malik identifies maʿun as the bucket, pot, and axe.
TAB-FULL:v24p677/r5.anchor: عن أبي مالك، في قول الله: " {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: الدلو والقدر والفأس "

TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r1.claim: Abdullah reports that the Prophet's Companions understood withholding maʿun as refusing a bucket and similar useful objects.
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي وائل، عن عبد الله، قال: " كنا مع نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم ونحن نقول: {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] : منع الدلو وأشباه ذلك "

TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb interprets maʿun as recognized good or kindness.

TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r3.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib says maʿun means money in the Quraysh dialect.
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن شهاب، عن سعيد بن المسيب، قال: " الماعون، بلسان قريش: المال "

TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r4.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri also says maʿun means money in the Quraysh dialect.
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي ذئب، عن الزهري، قال: " الماعون: بلسان قريش: المال "

TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the general sense that they withhold useful things people lend one another and the rights God assigns to the poor and needy in their wealth, since the verse does not restrict what they withhold.
TAB-FULL:v24p677#2/r5.anchor: أن الله وصفهم بأنهم يمنعون الناس ما يتعاورونه بينهم، ويمنعون أهل الحاجة والمسكنة ما أوجب الله لهم في أموالهم من الحقوق

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: Q 68:12 and 70:21 provide parallels for withholding good or help.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. 68:12 (mannāʿin li-l-ḫairi muʿtadin ʾaṯīm) und 70:21 (wa-ʾiḏā massahu l-ḫairu manūʿā)

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Geiger
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r2.claim: Geiger derives māʿūn from Hebrew māʿôn, meaning dwelling or refuge, and interprets the verse as denying shelter to people seeking help.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Geiger leitet den Ausdruck māʿūn von hebr. māʿôn, „Wohnung“ und auch „Zuflucht“, her

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Nöldeke
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r3.claim: Nöldeke accepts Geiger's derivation but rejects the assumption that Arabic must preserve the Hebrew word's original meaning.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Nöldeke (1910, 28) akzeptiert Geigers Ableitung, lehnt jedoch die Annahme ab

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Nöldeke
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.claim: Nöldeke cites al-Aʿshā Maimūn's verse praising someone as more generous with his benefits than a foaming Euphrates channel, supporting the sense benefit or gift.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.anchor: einen Vers von al-Aʿšā Maimūn, in dem es über den Gelobten heißt

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.claim: The Hebrew loan māʿūn apparently already meant benefit, gift, or donation in pre-Qur'anic Arabic.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Der ursprünglich aus dem Hebräischen stammende Ausdruck māʿūn hatte also offenbar bereits in vorkoranischer Zeit die Bedeutung „Wohltat“, „Spende“ o. Ä. angenommen

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.speaker: Rhodokanakis
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.claim: Rhodokanakis agrees with Nöldeke and explains the Arabic semantic development through interference from maʿūna, from root ʿ-w-n.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.anchor: Rhodokanakis angeschlossen, der die eigenständige Bedeutungsentwicklung von arab. māʿūn durch Interferenz mit arab. maʿūna

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.claim: A deliberate Qur'anic echo of Hebrew māʿôn remains possible despite the Arabic word's changed meaning.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Gleichwohl ist nicht auszuschließen, daß die koranische Verwendung des Ausdrucks bewußt den Anklang an hebräisch māʿôn sucht

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r3.claim: The closing verse adds refusal of assistance, generalizing the earlier failure to support orphans and the poor, who represent socially vulnerable people in the Hebrew Bible.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r3.anchor: Die am Ende der ersten Versgruppe exemplarisch angeführte Unterlassung der Unterstützung besonders schwacher Gesellschaftsmitglieder

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.claim: The two groups cross-correspond: verse 1 and verses 4–6 concern religious omissions, while verses 2–3 and verse 7 concern social omissions; the first group stresses social failings and the second religious ones.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.anchor: Inhaltlich korrespondieren insofern V. 1 und V. 4–6 (religiöse Unterlassungen) und V. 2.3 und V. 7 (soziale Unterlassungen)

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r5.claim: Māʿūn and manaʿa are near-anagrams built from permutations of the same consonants, m-n-ʿ and m-ʿ-n.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r5.anchor: die zwei unterschiedliche Permutationen desselben Konsonantenbestandes (m-n-ʿ / m-ʿ-n) enthalten

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r6.claim: The rare hapax māʿūn was likely chosen instead of a commoner word for its assonance with manaʿa; the sound pattern sharpens the contrast between expected assistance and its denial, a figure later rhetoricians call reversed paronomasia.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r6.anchor: in der Terminologie späterer Rhetoriker handelt es sich um die Stilfigur des ǧinās maqlūb

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.claim: The surah warns people professing religion whose traits resemble hypocrites: neglecting prayer, acting ostentatiously, and withholding aid, all incompatible with belief in requital.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.anchor: بيان وعيد لمن كان من المنتحلين بالدين متخلقا بأخلاق المنافقين

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.claim: The surah may be Meccan or Medinan; another view says its first half is Meccan and second half Medinan.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية، وقيل نصفها مكي ونصفها مدني

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r13.claim: Ma'un is anything that helps another meet a need, such as a loan, a good deed, or lending household goods; this common meaning underlies the different reported definitions.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r13.anchor: الماعون كل ما يعين الغير في رفع حاجة من حوائج الحياة كالقرض تقرضه والمعروف تصنعه

TABATABAI:107:5-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r4.claim: A Prophetic report identifies ma'un as tools people help each other with, including an axe, cooking pot, bucket, and similar items.
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { ويمنعون الماعون } قال " ما تعاون الناس بينهم الفاس

TABATABAI:107:5-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r5.claim: A report from Abu Abd Allah defines ma'un as a loan, good deed, household goods lent, and zakat.
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r5.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث قال وقوله عز وجل { ويمنعون الماعون } هو القرض تقرضه

TABATABAI:107:5-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r6.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r6.claim: Sunni reports also explain ma'un as obligatory zakat, connecting prayer-showing with withholding zakat.
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r6.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام كما في الدر المنثور ولفظه الماعون الزكاة المفروضة

TABATABAI:107:5-7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r7.claim: The Prophet describes ma'un as stone, iron, water, and similar items; another report specifies copper cooking pots and axe iron, and stone pots.
TABATABAI:107:5-7/r7.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الحجر والحديد والماء وأشباه ذلك

TABRISI:107:5-7/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r12.speaker: علي، ابن عمر، الحسن، قتادة، الضحاك، أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:107:5-7/r12.claim: These authorities identify al-ma'un as the obligatory alms, a view also transmitted from Abu Abdillah.
TABRISI:107:5-7/r12.anchor: هي الزكاة المفروضة عن علي وابن عمر والحسن وقتادة والضحاك وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله ع

TABRISI:107:5-7/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:107:5-7/r13.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr interpret al-ma'un as commonly shared useful items such as buckets, axes, and pots, including things rarely withheld like water and salt; a raised report is also given.
TABRISI:107:5-7/r13.anchor: ما يتعاوره الناس بينهم من الدلو والفأس والقدر وما لا يمنع كالماء والملح عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وروي ذلك مرفوعا

TABRISI:107:5-7/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r14.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:107:5-7/r14.claim: Abu Abdillah, in Abu Basir's report, defines al-ma'un as a loan, a good deed, lending household goods, and alms.
TABRISI:107:5-7/r14.anchor: أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله ع قال هو القرض تقرضه والمعروف تصنعه ومتاع البيت تعيره ومنه الزكاة

TABRISI:107:5-7/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:107:5-7/r15.claim: Abu Abdillah says there is no blame in refusing to lend household goods to neighbors who break or damage them.
TABRISI:107:5-7/r15.anchor: ليس عليك جناح أن تمنعهم إذا كانوا كذلك

TABRISI:107:5-7/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:107:5-7/r16.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:107:5-7/r16.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets al-ma'un as all good deeds.

THALABI:v10p305/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r6.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p305/r6.claim: He identifies al-maʿun as obligatory alms; Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibn al-Hanafiya, and al-Dahhak share this interpretation.
THALABI:v10p305/r6.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه ويمنعون الماعون قال: هي الزكاة

THALABI:v10p305/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r7.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v10p305/r7.claim: He says al-maʿun means everyday tools such as an axe, bucket, cooking pot, and similar useful items.
THALABI:v10p305/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله في الماعون قال: الفاس والدلو والقدر وأشباه ذلك

THALABI:v10p305/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p305/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Saeed ibn Jubayr interprets al-maʿun as borrowed goods and household utensils.
THALABI:v10p305/r8.anchor: وهي رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس، مجاهد عنه: هو العارية ومتاع البيت

THALABI:v10p305/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p305/r9.claim: Through Atiyya, Ibn Abbas is also said to interpret al-maʿun as obedience.

THALABI:v10p305/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r10.speaker: محمد بن كعب والكلبي
THALABI:v10p305/r10.claim: They say al-maʿun is all customary kindness and help people exchange with one another.
THALABI:v10p305/r10.anchor: محمد بن كعب والكلبي: الماعون المعروف كله الذي يتعاطاه الناس فيما بينهم

THALABI:v10p305/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري ومقاتل
THALABI:v10p305/r11.claim: They say al-maʿun means wealth in Quraysh’s dialect; al-Aʿsha’s poem supports this lexical meaning.
THALABI:v10p305/r11.anchor: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري ومقاتل: الماعون: المال بلغة قريش، قال الأعشى

THALABI:v10p306/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p306/r1.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p306/r1.claim: He cites an Arab expression in which al-maʿun means obedience and compliance, illustrated by an unknown poet’s verse.
THALABI:v10p306/r1.anchor: تعطيك الماعون، أي الطاعة والانقياد، قال الشاعر

THALABI:v10p306/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p306/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p306/r2.claim: He also reports that some Arabs use maʿun for flowing water.
THALABI:v10p306/r2.anchor: وحكى الفراء أيضا عن بعضهم أنه قال: ماعون من الماء المعين

THALABI:v10p306/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p306/r3.speaker: قطرب
THALABI:v10p306/r3.claim: He derives the word from scarcity: maʿun names alms, charity, and kindness because they are a small part of much wealth.
THALABI:v10p306/r3.anchor: وقال قطرب: أصل الماعون من القلة، يقول العرب: ماله سعنة ولا معنة

THALABI:v10p306/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p306/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p306/r4.claim: Another view says al-maʿun means things that must not be withheld, such as water, salt, and fire.
THALABI:v10p306/r4.anchor: وقيل: الماعون ما لا يحل منعه مثل الماء والملح والنار

THALABI:v10p306/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p306/r5.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p306/r5.claim: In a report from Aisha, the Prophet says water, salt, and fire should not be withheld; sharing fire or salt earns the equivalent of what is cooked or seasoned, and giving water is likened to freeing sixty people or saving a life.
THALABI:v10p306/r5.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: يا رسول الله ما الذي لا يحل منعه قال: «الماء والملح والنار»

THALABI:v10p306/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p306/r6.speaker: الراعي
THALABI:v10p306/r6.claim: His poem describes a people who do not withhold their help or the confession of God’s oneness.
THALABI:v10p306/r6.anchor: قال الراعي: قوم على الإسلام لما يمنعوا … ماعونهم ويمنعوا التهليلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, and Ali interpret al-maʿun as the alms due on their wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p360/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد زكاة أموالهم (¬5). وهو قول علي

WAHIDI-QT:107:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:107:7/r1.claim: Al-maʿun means alms and useful objects such as an axe, pot, water, or salt.
WAHIDI-QT:107:7/r1.anchor: الزكاة وما فيه منفعة من الفأس والقدر والماء والملح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r5.claim: The withheld aid includes zakat and useful items such as an axe, pot, water, or salt.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:107:1-7/r5.anchor: { ويمنعون الماعون } الزكاة وما فيه منفعة من الفأس والقدر والماء والملح.

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.claim: The context includes people who perform a few prayers smugly as if religion consisted only of them, neglecting other duties such as almsgiving and help for God's servants.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.anchor: kıldıkları birkaç vakit namazdan dolayı mağrur olup yanılıp da din ondan ibaret imiş gibi sâir ibadet ve ubûdiyet vazifelerini yapmayanlar da dâhil olur

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly pairs prayer with zakat as foundational righteous duties after faith; some who seem devout wrongly neglect financial obligations.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.anchor: Kur’an’da imandan sonra sâlih amellerin esası olmak üzere namaz ve zekât beraber zikrolunagelmiştir

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.claim: Mosques are maintained by those who believe in God and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear only God.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.anchor: إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.claim: Prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing; people who persist in these and refuse aid have ignored prayer's admonition and meaning.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.anchor: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r17.claim: Al-maʿūn may mean zakat, or even the smallest customary loan or assistance; those who withhold such minor help would all the more withhold zakat.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r17.anchor: mâ‘ûnu men ederler zekâtı vermezler, yahut kimsenin esirgemeyeceği âriyet gibi cüz’î bir yardımlığı bile sakınır

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.claim: Religious pretenders who neglect prayer, show off, and withhold even small help are more astonishingly blameworthy than disbelievers who deny religion and mistreat orphans and the poor.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.anchor: namaz kılar dindar görünüp de namazlarından yanılan, mürâîlik, gösteriş yapıp

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.claim: After the address to the Prophet to see and understand, Sūrat al-Kawthar condenses the preceding suras, especially those from al-Ḍuḥā, as a final account of Muhammad's rank.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.anchor: Ve’d-Duhâ’dan beri gelen sûrelerin mazmûnu üzerinde hepsinin tetimmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.claim: After condemning failure in one's duties toward people, the surah criticizes those who fail to fulfill genuine duties of worship toward God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.anchor: Yukarıda insanlara karşı insanlık görevini yerine getirmeyenler kınanmıştı; burada ise Allah’a karşı gerçek anlamda kulluk görevlerini yerine getirmeyenler eleştirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.claim: Three faults are given among people who pray: distance from prayer's essence, ostentation in worship, and obstructing good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.anchor: Namazlarının özünden uzak olmaları, b) İbadetlerinde halka gösteriş yapmaları, c) Hayra engel olmaları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.claim: Tabari reports that ma'un has been explained as alms, other financial duties, benefits people withhold from each other, a right, a loan, or property.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.anchor: zekât, diğer malî yükümlülükler, insanların kendi aralarında birbirine yararlandırmadıkları nimetler, hak, ödünç, mal

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.claim: Tabari understands ma'un broadly as kindness, good, and sharing benefits; the authors likewise render it with the broad word “good.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.anchor: insanlara iyilik, hayır, nimetlerin paylaşılması gibi anlamları kuşatan genel bir ifade olduğunu belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.claim: The surah stresses that sincere worship of God and mutual aid and solidarity cannot be separated in religious devotion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.anchor: Allah’a gönülden ibadet etmekle yardımlaşma ve dayanışmanın dindarlıkta birbirinden ayrılmazlığının vurgulanmış olması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.claim: A truly believing person fulfills duties toward God and creation sincerely, does good, and enables rather than blocks its spread through social cooperation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.anchor: yardımlaşma ve dayanışmanın önünü tıkayan değil, aksine gelişip yaygınlaşmasına, bireyselliği aşarak toplumsal ve kurumsal bir yapı kazanmasına katkıda bulunan insandır

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3467#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3467#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3467#2/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud says al-ma'un includes borrowed household tools such as pots, scales, and buckets.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3467#2/r4.anchor: حدثنا أبي ، حدثنا عفان ، حدثنا حماد بن سلمة عن عاصم عن زر ، عن عبد الله قال : الماعون العواري القدر والميزان والدلو

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says al-ma'un in the Prophet's time included lending a bucket, pot, axe, scales, and ordinary items people share.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3469/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : كنا نعد الماعون على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عارية الدلو والقدر والفاس والميزان

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r11.speaker: علي، وابن عمر، وابن الحنفية، والحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r11.anchor: قيل: هي الزكاة الواجبة، عن علي، وابن عمر، وابن الحنفية، والحسن

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وابن عمر، وسعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r12.claim: Al-ma'un is the shared household gear people lend one another, such as an axe, pot, or bucket.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r12.anchor: الماعون: ما يتداوله الناس بينهم من الفأس، والقدر، والدلو

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r13.claim: Al-ma'un can mean ordinary household items borrowed by neighbors; Abu Ali says this portrays extreme stinginess and baseness.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r13.anchor: هو ما يسأله الجيران بعضهم من بعض من الأمتعة التي يستعيرها الناس

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r14.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r14.claim: A report repeatedly identifies al-ma'un as zakat and urges people to pay it to be saved; the author prefers this because abandoning zakat merits the threat.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r14.anchor: وروي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: الماعون الزكاة - أربع مرات

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r15.claim: Lending was obligatory at the beginning of Islam because the emigrants were poor, then became permissible as circumstances improved.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r15.anchor: كانت العارية واجبة في ابتداء الإسلام لضيق ذات يد المهاجرين

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r16.claim: The verse condemns their low character because they would not help vulnerable believers.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r16.anchor: ذم هؤلاء لأنهم لخستهم لا يعينون ضعفاء المؤمنين

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r17.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب، والزهري، ومقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r17.claim: In Qurayshi usage, al-ma'un means wealth.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r17.anchor: الماعون بلسان قريش: المال، عن سعيد بن المسيب، والزهري، ومقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r18.claim: Another interpretation defines al-ma'un as obedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r18.anchor: وقيل: هو الطاعة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v10p7559/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r19.speaker: محمد بن كعب، والكلبي
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r19.claim: Another interpretation defines al-ma'un as all good deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7559/r19.anchor: وقيل: هو المعروف كله، عن محمد بن كعب، والكلبي

MAJAZ:v2p313/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p313/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p313/r2.claim: In pre-Islamic usage al-māʿūn means every benefit or gift; al-Aʿshā’s line witnesses the word.
MAJAZ:v2p313/r2.anchor: «يمنعون الماعون» (7) هو فى الجاهلية كل منفعة وعطية، قال الأعشى: بأجود منه بماعونه ... إذا ما سماؤهم لم تغم [947]

MAJAZ:v2p313/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p313/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p313/r3.claim: In Islam al-māʿūn means obedience and alms; al-Rāʿī’s verse uses it in that sense.
MAJAZ:v2p313/r3.anchor: والماعون فى الإسلام الطاعة والزكاة قال الراعي: قوم على الإسلام لما يمنعوا ... ما عونهم ويضيعوا التنزيلا

MAJAZ:v2p313/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p313/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p313/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda recounts that a man said his camel Ṣafiyya would give him māʿūn, meaning that it would submit or obey.
MAJAZ:v2p313/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: وكانت لى ناقة صفية فقال لى رجل: لو قد نزلنا لقد صنعت بناقتك صنيعا تعطيك الماعون أي تنقاد.

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.claim: Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.anchor: وإن كانت السورة كلها وحدة متماسكة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.claim: The seven short verses overturn conventional ideas of faith and disbelief and reveal the creed’s mercy and immense good for humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة الصغيرة ذات الآيات السبع القصيرة تعالج حقيقة ضخمة تكاد تبدل المفهوم السائد للإيمان والكفر

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.claim: Religion is an integrated way of life whose worship, rites, and personal and social duties purify hearts and lead people to cooperation, care, and flourishing.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.anchor: إنما هو منهج متكامل ، تتعاون عباداته وشعائره

QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.claim: Those heedless worshippers are the ones who show off and withhold small acts of help.

TAB:107:4/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:4/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are hypocrites who display prayer before people, abandon it when unseen, and withhold borrowed household goods.
TAB:107:4/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : { فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } فهم المنافقون كانوا يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar defines maʿūn as withholding what is due; he rejects reducing it to lending small household items such as an axe and bucket.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r1.anchor: سألت عبد الله بن عمر عن {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] ؟ قال: هو منع الحق

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿUmar identifies maʿūn as zakāt.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: «هي الزكاة» حدثنا ابن حميد،

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r3.claim: A report from ʿAlī likewise identifies maʿūn as zakāt.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r3.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي صالح، عن علي، مثله

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says maʿūn means zakāt.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r4.anchor: عن حسان بن مخارق، عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " {الماعون} [الماعون: 7] الزكاة "

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r5.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r5.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan say maʿūn is the obligatory zakāt.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، والحسن: " الماعون: الزكاة المفروضة "

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya identifies maʿūn as zakāt.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r6.anchor: عن ابن الحنفية، رضي الله عنه قال: «هي الزكاة»

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r7.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: «الزكاة»

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the hypocrites withhold the zakāt due on their wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: «هم المنافقون يمنعون زكاة أموالهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r9.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they withheld alms from their wealth, for which God censured them.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r9.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول: " {ويمنعون الماعون} [الماعون: 7] قال: «منعوا صدقات أموالهم، فعاب الله عليهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that the hypocrite withholds zakāt, prays for display, and feels no regret if he misses prayer.
TAB-FULL:v24p670/r10.anchor: عن الحسن، " {الذين هم يراءون ويمنعون الماعون}

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.claim: If verses 6–7 are combined despite the rhyme potential at yurāʾūn, the sura has a symmetrical structure of two triads.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:6:anmerkung/r2.anchor: so ergibt sich für Sure 107 ein symmetrischer Aufbau von zwei Dreiergruppen

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.claim: Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.anchor: مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث ، فإنه يجزئ المكذب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.claim: The four names plainly signal the surah's subject: it explicitly forbids vices and implicitly urges noble conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.anchor: وكل من اسمائها الأربعة في غاية الظهور في الدلالة على ذلك بتأمل السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.claim: Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.anchor: إن هذه كلها من شأن المكذب بالحساب والجزاء لأن نفع البعد عنها إنما يكون إذ ذاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p547#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p547#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p547#2/r1.claim: Al-Māʿūn forbids base manners and ends with stingy withholding; al-Kawthar answers with generous giving to the noblest recipient, urging virtue and distinguishing the Prophet from those warnings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p547#2/r1.anchor: وكانت الدين قد ختمت بأبخل البخلاء وأدنى الخلائق : المنع تنفيرا من البخل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.claim: The commands answer al-Māʿūn's four vices: giving counters stinginess, prayer counters neglect, exclusive devotion counters ostentation, and sacrifice counters withholding alms.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p548/r8.anchor: وقد قابل في هذا أربعا من سورة الدين بأربع , وهي البخل بالإعطاء , وإضاعة الصلاة بالأمر بها

DURR-FULL:v8p642/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p642/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p642/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿud says al-maʿun meant everyday items people lent one another, such as a bucket, pot, axe, or scale.
DURR-FULL:v8p642/r12.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: كنا نعد الماعون على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عارية الدلو والقدر

TAB:107:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:107:7/r1.claim: They deny people the benefits of what they possess.
TAB:107:7/r1.anchor: يقول :  ويمنعون الناس منافع ما عندهم

TAB:107:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r2.speaker: author
TAB:107:7/r2.claim: The basic sense of al-maʿūn is the benefit of anything; rainwater descending from clouds is also called maʿūn.
TAB:107:7/r2.anchor: وأصل الماعون من كلّ شيء منفعته ،

TAB:107:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r3.speaker: author
TAB:107:7/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites al-Aʿshā ibn Thaʿlaba’s line as poetic evidence for maʿūn as rainwater.
TAB:107:7/r3.anchor: بأَجْوَدَ مِنْهُ بِمَاعُونِهِ *** إذَا ما سَماؤُهُمُ لَمْ تَغِمْ

TAB:107:7/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r4.speaker: author
TAB:107:7/r4.claim: An unnamed poet describes a cloud pouring maʿūn, another poetic use for rainwater.
TAB:107:7/r4.anchor:
وقال آخر يصف سحابا :
*** يَمُجّ صَبِيرُهُ المَاعُونَ صَبّا ***

TAB:107:7/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r5.speaker: author
TAB:107:7/r5.claim: In ʿUbayd al-Rāʿī’s poem, maʿūn means obedience and zakat.

TAB:107:7/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r6.speaker: عليّ
TAB:107:7/r6.claim: Mujāhid reports that ʿAlī interpreted al-maʿūn as the obligatory zakat.
TAB:107:7/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  قال عليّ رضي الله عنه ،   في قوله :  {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  الزكاة .

TAB:107:7/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB:107:7/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar defines al-maʿūn as wealth whose due right is withheld.
TAB:107:7/r7.anchor: سأل رجل ابن عمر عن الماعون ،   قال :  هو المال الذي لا يؤدّى حقه .

TAB:107:7/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB:107:7/r8.claim: When told that Ibn Masʿūd meant loaned household tools, Ibn ʿUmar insists that his definition of al-maʿūn as withheld rights is correct.
TAB:107:7/r8.anchor: فإن ابن مسعود يقول :  هو الفأس والقدر ،   قال ابن عمر :  هو ما أقول لك .

TAB:107:7/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB:107:7/r9.claim: A report also gives Ibn ʿUmar’s concise gloss of al-maʿūn as zakat.
TAB:107:7/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال :  هي الزكاة .

TAB:107:7/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB:107:7/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identifies al-maʿūn as zakat.
TAB:107:7/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جُبير ،   قال :  المَاعُونَ :  الزكاة .

TAB:107:7/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r11.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB:107:7/r11.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan say al-maʿūn is the prescribed zakat.
TAB:107:7/r11.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن :  الماعون :  الزكاة المفروضة .

TAB:107:7/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r12.speaker: ابن الحنفية
TAB:107:7/r12.claim: Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya interprets al-maʿūn as zakat.
TAB:107:7/r12.anchor: عن ابن الحنفية رضي الله عنه قال :  هي الزكاة .

TAB:107:7/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r13.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:107:7/r13.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also says al-maʿūn is zakat.
TAB:107:7/r13.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  الزكاة .

TAB:107:7/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:107:7/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says the hypocrites withhold the zakat on their wealth.
TAB:107:7/r14.anchor: قال ابن زيد ، في قوله :  {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  هم المنافقون يمنعون زكاة أموالهم .

TAB:107:7/r15.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r15.speaker: الحسن
TAB:107:7/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they withheld the charities due on their wealth, for which God censured them.
TAB:107:7/r15.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول :  {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  منعوا صدقات أموالهم ، فعاب الله عليهم .

TAB:107:7/r16.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r16.speaker: الحسن
TAB:107:7/r16.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes the hypocrite who withholds zakat: he performs prayer ostentatiously and feels no regret when he misses it.
TAB:107:7/r16.anchor: عن الحسن {  الّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  هو المنافق الذي يمنع زكاة ماله ، فإن صلى رأى ، وإن فاتته لم يأس عليها .

TAB:107:7/r17.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB:107:7/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reports identify al-maʿūn as useful tools people lend one another, especially an axe, pot, or bucket; one account says at least two of the three.
TAB:107:7/r17.anchor: عن أبي وائل ،   عن عبد الله ،   قال :  كنا مع نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم ونحن نقول :  الماعون :  منع الدلو وأشباه ذلك .

TAB:107:7/r18.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r18.speaker: أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:107:7/r18.claim: The Prophet’s Companions are reported to have called an axe, bucket, and pot among the items meant by al-maʿūn.
TAB:107:7/r18.anchor: عن أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   قالوا :  إن من الماعون :  الفأس والدلو والقدر .

TAB:107:7/r19.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:7/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to gloss al-maʿūn as a loan, household goods, or items people circulate among themselves.
TAB:107:7/r19.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله :  {  الماعون } قال :  متاع البيت .

TAB:107:7/r20.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:7/r20.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās notes that interpreters differed, listing zakat, obedience, and loaned property as proposed meanings.
TAB:107:7/r20.anchor: عن ابن عباس {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  اختلف الناس في ذلك ، فمنهم من قال :  يمنعون الزكاة ، ومنهم من قال :  يمنعون الطاعة

TAB:107:7/r21.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:7/r21.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the people entitled to the item have not yet come for it.
TAB:107:7/r21.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس ، في قوله :  {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  لم يجىء أهلها بعد .

TAB:107:7/r22.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r22.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB:107:7/r22.claim: In another reported interpretation, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says al-maʿūn means a loaned item.
TAB:107:7/r22.anchor: عن سعيد بن جُبير قال :  المَاعُونَ :  العارية .

TAB:107:7/r23.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r23.speaker: عليّ
TAB:107:7/r23.claim: ʿAlī is also reported to combine the meanings: al-maʿūn includes withheld zakat and everyday tools such as an axe, bucket, and pot.
TAB:107:7/r23.anchor: قال عليّ رضي الله عنه :  الماعون :  منع الزكاة والفأس والدلو والقدر .

TAB:107:7/r24.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r24.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB:107:7/r24.claim: Abū Mālik identifies al-maʿūn as a bucket, pot, and axe.
TAB:107:7/r24.anchor: عن أبي مالك ، في قول الله :  {  وَيَمْنَعُونَ المَاعُونَ } قال :  الدلو والقدر والفأس .

TAB:107:7/r25.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r25.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:107:7/r25.claim: Ibrāhīm says al-maʿūn is the borrowing of household items such as an axe, pot, and bucket.
TAB:107:7/r25.anchor: عن إبراهيم أنه قال :  هو عارية الناس :  الفأس والقدر والدلو ونحو ذلك ،

TAB:107:7/r26.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r26.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB:107:7/r26.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb interprets al-maʿūn as ordinary kindness or good deeds.
TAB:107:7/r26.anchor: سمعت محمد بن كعب يقول :  الماعون :  المعروف .

TAB:107:7/r27.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r27.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB:107:7/r27.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says that in Quraysh’s dialect al-maʿūn means wealth.
TAB:107:7/r27.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب ، قال :  الماعون ، بلسان قريش :  المال .

TAB:107:7/r28.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r28.speaker: الزهري
TAB:107:7/r28.claim: Al-Zuhrī likewise says that in Quraysh’s dialect al-maʿūn means wealth.
TAB:107:7/r28.anchor: عن الزهريّ ، قال :  الماعون :  بلسان قريش :  المال .

TAB:107:7/r29.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:7/r29.speaker: author
TAB:107:7/r29.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers a broad reading: they withhold both items people lend one another and the rights God assigned to the needy, since both are benefits people receive from one another.
TAB:107:7/r29.anchor: يمنعون الناس ما يتعاورونه بينهم ،   ويمنعون أهل الحاجة والمسكنة ما أوجب الله لهم في أموالهم من الحقوق ؛  لأن كلّ ذلك من المنافع

BURHAN:v1p38/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p38/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p38/r9.claim: The command to sacrifice answers al-Māʿūn’s charge of withholding help: the sacrificial meat is to be given in charity.
BURHAN:v1p38/r9.anchor: وفى مقابلة منع الماعون ﴿ وانحر ﴾ وأراد به التصدق بلحم الأضاحى

BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Surat al-Maun is Meccan except from فويل للمصلين through its end, which is Medinan.
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.anchor: سورة ﴿ أرأيت ﴾ مكية إلا قوله ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ إلى آخرها فإنها مدنية كذا قال مقاتل بن سليمان

BURHAN:v2p150/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r14.claim: One interpretation of al-maun is the obligatory alms tax.
BURHAN:v2p150/r14.anchor: ﴿ ويمنعون الماعون ﴾ قيل الزكاة المفروضة وقيل العارية

BURHAN:v2p150/r15.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r15.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r15.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is a loaned or borrowed item.
BURHAN:v2p150/r15.anchor: قيل العارية أو الماء أو النار أو الكلأ

BURHAN:v2p150/r16.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r16.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r16.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is water.
BURHAN:v2p150/r16.anchor: العارية أو الماء أو النار أو الكلأ أو الرفد

BURHAN:v2p150/r17.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r17.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r17.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is fire.
BURHAN:v2p150/r17.anchor: الماء أو النار أو الكلأ أو الرفد أو المغرفة

BURHAN:v2p150/r18.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r18.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r18.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is pasture or grazing land.
BURHAN:v2p150/r18.anchor: النار أو الكلأ أو الرفد أو المغرفة وكلها صحيح

BURHAN:v2p150/r19.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r19.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r19.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is assistance or support.
BURHAN:v2p150/r19.anchor: الكلأ أو الرفد أو المغرفة وكلها صحيح لأن مانع الكل آثم

BURHAN:v2p150/r20.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r20.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r20.claim: Another interpretation of al-maun is a ladle.
BURHAN:v2p150/r20.anchor: أو الرفد أو المغرفة وكلها صحيح لأن مانع الكل آثم

BURHAN:v2p150/r21.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p150/r21.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p150/r21.claim: Every cited meaning is valid, since withholding each of these items is sinful.
BURHAN:v2p150/r21.anchor: وكلها صحيح لأن مانع الكل آثم

ITQAN:v3p297/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.claim: Al-Kawthar counters al-Ma'un's four traits: abundant giving opposes miserliness, prayer opposes neglect, worship for God opposes showing off, and sacrifice meat is charity opposing withholding small kindnesses.
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.anchor: لأن السابقة وصف الله فيها المنافق بأربعة أمور البخل وترك الصلاة والرياء فيها ومنع الزكاة

ITQAN:v1p154/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p154/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p154/r12.claim: Surat Araayta is also called Surat al-Din and Surat al-Maun.
ITQAN:v1p154/r12.anchor: أرأيت تسمى سورة الدين وسورة الماعون

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r1.speaker: قطرب
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r1.claim: Quṭrub derives māʿūn as fāʿūl from maʿn, meaning a small thing; Arabs say mā lahu maʿn for someone with little.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r1.anchor: الماعون : فاعول من المعن ،   وهو الشيء القليل . تقول العرب : ما له معن ،   أي شيء قليل ،   وقاله قطرب

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r2.claim: An alternative derives it from maʿūna, with the alif compensating for tāʾ marbūṭa and mīm augmenting the original pattern.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r2.anchor: وقيل : أصله معونة والألف عوض من الهاء ،   فوزنه مفعل في الأصل على مكرم

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r3.claim: Another derivation makes māʿūn a passive participle of aʿāna, with metathesis and the same wāw-to-alif change as bawb to bāb.

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج والمبرد
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda, al-Zajjāj, and al-Mubarrad say pre-Islamic māʿūn meant any useful object, such as an axe, bucket, pot, or fire striker, whether little or much; in Islam it means obedience.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والزجاج والمبرد : الماعون في الجاهلية : كلما فيه منفعة حتى الفاس والدلو والقدر والقداحة

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r5.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r5.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse is cited as poetic evidence for māʿūn meaning a useful benefit.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r5.anchor: وأنشدوا بيت الأعشى : بأجود منه بماعونه *** إذا ما سماءهم لم تغم

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r6.speaker: ابن المسيب وابن شهاب
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r6.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib and Ibn Shihāb say māʿūn means wealth in Quraysh’s dialect.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r6.anchor: قال ابن المسيب وابن شهاب : الماعون ،   بلغة قريش : المال

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r7.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports from some Arabs that māʿūn means water.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء عن بعض العرب : الماعون : الماء

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن الحنفية والحسن والضحاك وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r8.claim: These authorities take māʿūn as the small household items people lend one another, such as an axe, bucket, or utensils.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r8.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن الحنفية والحسن والضحاك وابن زيد : ما يتعاطاه الناس بينهم ،   كالفأس والدلو والآنية

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r9.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet named water, salt, and fire as things that should not be withheld; some transmissions add a needle and leaven.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : « سئل صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشيء الذي لا يحل منعه فقال : الماء والملح والنار » وفي بعض الطرق : الإبرة والخمير

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r10.speaker: علي وابن عمر وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r10.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, and also Ibn ʿAbbās identify māʿūn as zakāt.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r10.anchor: وقال علي وابن عمر وابن عباس أيضا : الماعون : الزكاة

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r11.claim: Al-Rāʿī’s poem uses māʿūn for zakāt; the sense fits a small portion taken from much, as does other charity.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r11.anchor: يعني بالماعون : الزكاة ،   وهذا القول يناسبه ما ذكره قطرب من أن أصله من المعن ،   وهو الشيء القليل ،   فسميت الزكاة ماعوناً لأنها قليل من كثير

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also gives the meaning of a loaned object.

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r13.speaker: محمد بن كعب والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r13.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Kalbī gloss māʿūn as all good conduct.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r13.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب والكلبي : هو المعروف كله

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r14.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar identifies it as withholding a due right.
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r14.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر : منع الحق

ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:7/r15.claim: Another view identifies māʿūn as water and pasture.

ALUSI:107:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r1.speaker: علي ومحمد بن الحنفية وابن عباس وابن عمر وزيد بن أسلم والضحاك وعكرمة
ALUSI:107:7/r1.claim: ʿAlī, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and ʿIkrima interpret al-māʿūn as zakāt; al-Rāʿī's verse about withholding it supports this reading.
ALUSI:107:7/r1.anchor: أي الزكاة كما جاء عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابنه محمد بن الحنفية وابن عباس وابن عمر

ALUSI:107:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب والكلبي
ALUSI:107:7/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Kalbī explain al-māʿūn as all that is commonly recognized as good.
ALUSI:107:7/r2.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب والكلبي المعروف كله

ALUSI:107:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI:107:7/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says al-māʿūn is household equipment people lend one another, such as a pot, bucket, or axe; reports also transmit this from Ibn ʿAbbās, and several marfūʿ hadiths are cited.
ALUSI:107:7/r3.anchor: وأخرج جماعة عن ابن مسعود تفسيره بما يعاوره الناس بينهم من القدر والدلو والفاس

ALUSI:107:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r4.speaker: الحاكم
ALUSI:107:7/r4.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticated a report from Ibn ʿAbbās on the shared household items interpretation; other scholars also transmit marfūʿ reports on it.
ALUSI:107:7/r4.anchor: وجاء ذلك عن ابن عباس أيضاً في خبر رواه عنه الضياء في المختارة والحاكم وصححه

ALUSI:107:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r5.claim: Withholding a needed borrowed item may be legally forbidden when someone must borrow it from necessity, and is poor etiquette even without necessity.
ALUSI:107:7/r5.anchor: ومنع ذلك قد يكون محظوراً في الشريعة كما إذا استعير عن اضطرار وقبيحاً في المروءة

ALUSI:107:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r6.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI:107:7/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī says māʿūn means property in Quraysh usage, as transmitted by Ibn Abī Shayba.
ALUSI:107:7/r6.anchor: وهو على ما أخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن الزهري المال بلسان قريش

ALUSI:107:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج والمبرد
ALUSI:107:7/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda, al-Zajjāj, and al-Mubarrad say pre-Islamic usage meant anything useful, small or great; in Islam it refers to obedience.
ALUSI:107:7/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والزجاج والمبرد هو في الجاهلية كل ما فيه منفعة من قليل أو كثير

ALUSI:107:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r8.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI:107:7/r8.claim: Quṭrub derives māʿūn from maʿn, meaning a small thing, as in the phrase mā lahu maʿna, he has a little something.
ALUSI:107:7/r8.anchor: فقال قطرب أصله فاعول من المعن وهو الشيء القليل

ALUSI:107:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r9.claim: Another etymology derives the word from maʿūna, with the alif replacing hāʾ; the original pattern is mufʿil.
ALUSI:107:7/r9.anchor: وقيل أصله معونة والألف عوض من الهاء فوزنه مفعل في الأصل

ALUSI:107:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r10.claim: A third analysis makes māʿūn a passive noun from aʿāna yuʿīnu, explaining its sound changes and pattern as maʿfūl.
ALUSI:107:7/r10.anchor: وقيل هو اسم مفعول من أعان يعين وأصله معوون فقلبت

ALUSI:107:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r11.claim: The fāʾ in fa-wayl is consequential: the discourse escalates from orphan-pushing to prayer-neglect, ostentation, and withholding zakāt or customary loans, increasingly exposing denial of religion.
ALUSI:107:7/r11.anchor: جزائية والكلام ترق من ذلك المعرف إلى معرف أقوى

ALUSI:107:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r12.claim: The sūra intensifies warning against these widespread vices as signs of denying religion; believers should flee them, since denial of religion lies behind every sin.
ALUSI:107:7/r12.anchor: والغرض التغليظ في أمر هذه الرذائل التي ابتلي بها كثير من الناس

ALUSI:107:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91.
ALUSI:107:7/r17.anchor: فكأنه قيل أخبرني ما تقول فيمن يكذبون بالدين وفيمن يؤذون اليتيم

ALUSI:107:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r18.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:107:7/r18.claim: Some make the fāʾ causal from the preceding coordination, requiring the worshippers and deniers to be one group; they are then identified as hypocrites, a reading reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Mālik, and supported by the ostentation clause.
ALUSI:107:7/r18.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الفاء في فويل على العطف المذكور للسببية وهذا الوجه يقتضي اتحاد المصلين والمكذبين

BAGHAWI:107:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r1.speaker: علي، ابن عمر، الحسن، قتادة، الضحاك
BAGHAWI:107:7/r1.claim: Ali, Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak identify al-māʿūn as zakat.
BAGHAWI:107:7/r1.anchor: روي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال : هي الزكاة ، وهو قول ابن عمر ، والحسن ، وقتادة والضحاك

BAGHAWI:107:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI:107:7/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies al-māʿūn as everyday items such as an axe, bucket, and cooking pot; a report from Ibn Abbas through Saʿid ibn Jubayr gives the same view.
BAGHAWI:107:7/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود : { الماعون } الفأس ، والدلو ، والقدر ، وأشباه ذلك

BAGHAWI:107:7/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI:107:7/r3.claim: Mujahid says al-māʿūn means a loan of something for use.

BAGHAWI:107:7/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI:107:7/r4.claim: Ikrima says its broadest instance is the obligatory zakat and its least is lending household goods.
BAGHAWI:107:7/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة : أعلاها الزكاة المعروفة ، وأدناها عارية المتاع

BAGHAWI:107:7/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب، الكلبي
BAGHAWI:107:7/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Kalbi take al-māʿūn as customary acts of kindness exchanged among people.
BAGHAWI:107:7/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب والكلبي : { الماعون } المعروف الذي يتعاطاه الناس فيما بينهم

BAGHAWI:107:7/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r6.speaker: قطرب
BAGHAWI:107:7/r6.claim: Qutrub derives the word from scarcity: it names zakat, charity, and kindness because each is a small portion of a larger amount.
BAGHAWI:107:7/r6.anchor: قال قطرب : أصل الماعون من القلة ، تقول العرب : ما له : سعة ولا منعة ، أي شيء قليل

BAGHAWI:107:7/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:7/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:107:7/r7.claim: One view says al-māʿūn is something it is unlawful to withhold, such as water, salt, or fire.
BAGHAWI:107:7/r7.anchor: وقيل : { الماعون } ما لا يحل منعه ، مثل : الماء ، والملح ، والنار

BAYDAWI:107:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:7/r1.claim: Al-māʿūn means the alms tax, or items customarily lent from one person to another.
BAYDAWI:107:7/r1.anchor: الزكاة أو ما يتعاور في العادة

BAYDAWI:107:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:7/r2.claim: The fāʾ introduces the consequence clause.
BAYDAWI:107:7/r2.anchor: والفاء جزائية ، والمعنى إذا كان عدم المبالاة باليتيم من ضعف الدين

BAYDAWI:107:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
